boardModes.growth: Growth Mode — the default. No ranks shown. The class sees the Spotlight Wall (badges), and every student privately sees their own scores, personal best and improvement. Nobody is ever shown as 'last'.
boardModes.podium: Podium Mode — only the top 3 appear on the shared board. Everyone else is listed alphabetically as a participant, with no scores shown.
boardModes.full: Full Mode — classic leaderboard with ranks and every score visible. Use only if the class voted for it.

categories.goal: Goal Completion — you delivered EVERY piece the brief asked for. Nothing missing.
categories.craft: Craft & Quality — your work is neat, formatted properly, realistic, and consistent.
categories.creativity: Creativity — original, specific ideas. Things the AI would NOT give everyone.
categories.technical: Technical Correctness — you used the month's tools and rules the right way.
categories.process: Process Evidence — you pasted your prompts, traces and logs. Proof of steps, not vibes.
categories.time: Time Discipline — the server clock decides this one. Before the buzzer = 10. Late = less. No submission = 0. The AI never grades time.

rules.scaleNote: Each category is scored 0–10. Total per day = 60. You are graded against the brief — not against each other.
rules.latePolicy: Submitted before the buzzer = 10. Late by 15 min or less = 7. Late by 16–30 min = 5. Late by 31–60 min = 3. Later than that = 1. No submission = 0. Finishing late still counts — submitting late is always better than not submitting.
rules.tieBreak: Ties are broken by Goal Completion first, then by who submitted earlier. (Instructor console always shows full ranks and scores.)
rules.badges: Every graded day hands out spotlight badges: Goal Getter, Craft Star, Creative Spark, Tech Whiz, Proof Pro, On-Time Champ, Most Improved, and Personal Best. Ties share the badge. You don't need to win the week to shine on a day.

days.title: The Prompt Sprint
days.tagline: Prompts only. No images, no code. One hour, one complete business starter pack.
days.skills: Month 1 — RBR, Chain-of-Thought, Few-Shot, self-checking AI, tables
days.mission: Today {business} has hired YOU as their AI consultant. Using ONLY text prompts in any chat AI, you will build their complete Business Starter Pack in 60 minutes.

simpleWords.meaning: Everything a new business needs to start talking to customers: a description, a price list, a promo plan, and a post.
Role-Background-Rules-Task — the 4-part prompt frame from Month 1. Give the AI a job, a story, rules, and a task.
Asking the AI to think step by step before answering, so the plan makes sense.
Showing the AI one example of what you want first, so it copies the style.
You paste your result back and ask the AI to find its own mistakes — then you show what it fixed.

steps: Read your assigned business below. Think for 2 minutes: who buys from them, and what problem do they solve?
Write ONE RBR prompt that produces a one-paragraph business description. The paragraph must name the customer and the problem.
Write a prompt that gives a price list of 3–5 items as a clean TABLE, with realistic Lagos 2026 prices in ₦.
Write a Chain-of-Thought prompt for a one-week WhatsApp promo plan — Monday to Saturday, one line per day.
Write a Few-Shot prompt for ONE ready-to-post social caption: give one example post first, then ask for the real one with a call to action.
Paste everything back and run ONE self-checking pass. The AI must find and fix at least one real mistake.
Paste ALL of it into the submit box: the four pieces, plus a heading called PROMPT LOG with every prompt you used, in order.
days.ifStuck: Copy the RBR skeleton from Month 1 Week 1: 'You are a... The background is... Your rules are... Your task is...' Fill in the blanks for your business.
days.ifEarly: Add a 7th piece: a customer complaint reply template using the same RBR voice. It counts for extra Craft points.
doneWhen: All four pieces exist — description, ₦ price table, 6-day promo plan, caption
PROMPT LOG is pasted under its own heading, with every prompt in order
The self-check shows at least one REAL correction — 'looks good' is not a correction
deliverables: Pieces 1–4 pasted in full (the price list as an actual table)
PROMPT LOG — every prompt, in order
The self-check: what the AI changed and why
caveats: Text prompts only — no image tools, no code tools today.
Prices must be realistic for Lagos in 2026 — no ₦500 laptops, no ₦2 million suya.
No reusing AminaStyle or any class example — your assigned business is your only subject.
The self-check must show at least one REAL change.
days.evidenceNote: The grading agent reads what you paste. Paste everything — the work AND the prompts.

days.title: Brand From Zero
days.tagline: A brand-new client. One hour. Logo, two matching product shots, one before/after.
days.skills: Month 2 — image prompts, style lock, inpainting / outpainting / retouching
days.mission: A brand-new client, {business}, needs a mini brand kit TODAY — a logo, two product shots that clearly belong together, and one before/after edit. In 60 minutes.

simpleWords.meaning: A small set of pictures that make a business look like ONE business: a logo plus product images in the same style.
The Month 2 trick for keeping the same look across images — repeating the same style words, or reusing the same reference image, so image #2 clearly belongs with image #1.
Editing INSIDE an image — like fixing or swapping one part only.
Growing the image — making the canvas bigger and letting the AI fill the new edges.
Cleaning up an image — sharper, better light, removing blemishes.

steps: Pick your client's identity in your head: one colour story, one mood. Write it down in one line — you will reuse those words in every prompt.
Generate the LOGO with one strong prompt.
Generate product/service image #1.
Generate image #2 with the SAME style words as image #1 — this is your style lock. The two must look like siblings, not strangers.
Choose one of your images and make a BEFORE/AFTER: inpaint something, outpaint the edges, or retouch it.
Attach all images, write one line describing each, and paste every prompt you used.
days.ifStuck: Reuse one exact style phrase in every prompt, e.g. 'flat vector logo style, kente gold and deep green, clean background'. Same phrase in, same family out.
days.ifEarly: Make a 3rd product shot that matches the pair — a harder consistency test — or write the brand's one-line slogan.
doneWhen: Logo + 2 matching product images + 1 before/after pair are attached
Every image has its prompt pasted — no orphan images
One line explains your style-lock trick for keeping the two product shots consistent
deliverables: All images attached (logo, 2 product shots, before/after)
One-line description under each image (the grading agent reads text; the human judge looks at files)
PROMPT LOG — the prompt for every image
Your style-lock explanation in one line
caveats: Brand-new identity only — no AminaStyle, no your own brand, no class assets.
The two product images must look like ONE brand — same style, same feel.
No real logos, no celebrity faces, no copyrighted characters.
The before/after must be a real edit of your own image — not two different generations.
Every image must come with the prompt that made it.
days.evidenceNote: The grading agent cannot see images — it grades your descriptions and prompt log. Attach files for the human judge, who can adjust scores.

days.title: The 30-Second Sell
days.tagline: Three clips, three lines of voice, one quiet beat. A 15–30 second advert.
days.skills: Month 2 — storyboarding, image-to-video, TTS voice-over, BGM, export
days.mission: Your client {business} needs a 15–30 second MP4 advert that sells ONE thing — today. Plan it, generate it, voice it, add music, and export it.

simpleWords.meaning: Your shot list written BEFORE you generate anything: what each shot shows, what moves, where the camera goes.
Starting a clip from a still image you already have, instead of from text only. More control.
Text-to-speech — the AI reads your script out loud with a generated voice.
Background music. Quiet. Under the voice. Generated by AI or genuinely royalty-free.
Text or a logo placed on top of the video.

steps: Write your 5-LINE storyboard: shot number, what it shows, subject motion, camera motion. Keep it simple — 5 shots is enough.
Write your 3-LINE voice script. Line 1 hooks, line 2 sells, line 3 tells them what to do.
Generate 2–3 clips from STILL IMAGES (image-to-video). Generate the images first if you don't have them.
Generate the TTS voice-over from your script. Re-generate if a word sounds wrong.
Generate quiet BGM — instrumental only, no famous songs.
Assemble: clips in order, voice on top, music under, ONE text or logo overlay. Check the volume: voice clear, music quiet.
Export ONE MP4 named brandname_advert.mp4 and check it measures 15–30 seconds.
days.ifStuck: Shorter is safer: 3 shots of 5 seconds each = 15 seconds, exactly in the window. Don't chase 30 seconds if time is tight.
days.ifEarly: Add a second overlay near the end with the client's phone number or location, or make a vertical 9:16 cut for WhatsApp Status.
doneWhen: One MP4 exists, measures 15–30 seconds, with voice + music + overlay
The 5-line storyboard and the 3-line voice script are pasted
The exact duration is stated and the file location (path or link) is given
deliverables: Storyboard (5 lines) pasted
Voice script (3 lines) pasted
PROMPT LOG — the clip prompts and the music prompt
The exact duration in seconds, and where the MP4 is saved (full path or link)
One screenshot or thumbnail attached, if you can
caveats: No famous songs — BGM must be AI-generated or genuinely royalty-free (the license rule).
The voice must be TTS, and the advert must actually measure 15–30 seconds.
At least two clips must start from still images (image-to-video), not pure text-to-video.
Volume balance: voice clear, music quiet — no drowning.
days.evidenceNote: The grading agent reads your storyboard, scripts, prompts and stated duration. Attach the thumbnail and give the file path for the human judge.

gradingFocus.craft: A tight edit — readable overlay, balanced audio, no dead seconds

days.title: Agent in a Box
days.tagline: Empty folder. Ninety minutes. One working agent with a gate that never lies.
days.skills: Month 3 — full-stack build, action cards, the Approve gate, step traces, .env
days.mission: Today's job: {business}. From an EMPTY folder, get your coding agent to build a working app where a customer request becomes a PENDING action card — and NOTHING happens until the owner clicks Approve or Reject.

simpleWords.meaning: A card that says 'here is what I want to do — waiting for your decision'. Status: PENDING until a human decides.
The class rule: nothing auto-sends, nothing charges money, nothing touches a real system. Only your click moves a card.
PLAN → use tool → CHECK → PROPOSE → STOP. The worker shows all five, in order, as a visible trace.
The step-by-step record of what the worker did. The exit ticket of Month 3: the trace, not a nicer reply.
Your product or pricing list is the ONLY thing the worker may state as fact. Unsure = 'not verified', never invented.

steps: Create an empty folder. Decide in one sentence what your worker does: which customer request becomes which card.
Write your scaffold prompt: describe the app, the PENDING card, the Approve/Reject buttons, and the five-step trace shown in the UI. Paste it to your coding agent.
Save the files exactly where the agent says. Put any API key in .env — variable names only in your paste, values hidden.
Run it. Open the app. Send one customer request.
Watch the trace: PLAN → use tool → CHECK → PROPOSE → STOP. A PENDING card must appear.
Click Approve, then test again and click Reject. The card's status must change — and nothing else must happen.
Paste your run instructions, your scaffold prompt, and the full five-step trace of your test request.
days.ifStuck: Say to your coding agent: 'Do all the wiring yourself, keep it to one page, no real sending anywhere.' Smaller app that works beats bigger app that doesn't.
days.ifEarly: Add a second card type (e.g. booking AND complaint) or a small history list showing decided cards.
doneWhen: The app runs from your run instructions
One full customer request produces a PENDING card
Approve and Reject work, and the five-step trace is visible in the UI
deliverables: What the app does — 3 lines
How to run it — the exact commands
PROMPT LOG — the scaffold prompt you gave the coding agent
A paste of the trace from one full customer request (all five steps)
If you used any API: proof your keys are in .env — paste the variable NAMES only, values hidden (e.g. MISTRAL_API_KEY=•••)
caveats: Any API key lives in .env — never in HTML, never pasted with its value.
The gate rule: nothing auto-sends, nothing charges, nothing touches a real system. Approve only changes the card's status.
Fresh scaffold — no reusing your class project files wholesale.
The trace must be visible in the app UI, not only in the console.
days.evidenceNote: The grading agent reads your run instructions, scaffold prompt and pasted trace. Keep your app open — the human judge may ask you to run it live.

days.title: Launch Day — Final Test
days.tagline: The certificate test. Two hours. One brand-new business launched from zero. No practice checks, no retakes.
days.skills: All 3 months — prompts, images, video/audio, prompt → HTML, presenting
days.mission: FINAL TEST (for your certificate): {business} launches TODAY. In 120 minutes you build the whole launch, then you pitch it live for 3 minutes. One submission only.

simpleWords.meaning: The Month 1 trick: describe the page in plain English, let the AI write ONE html file you can open offline.
The big first picture at the top of the page. First impression.
Five lines: what it is, who it's for, why now, the price, one proof. Spoken out loud, 3 minutes.

steps: Spend 5 minutes planning: who is the customer, what do they pay, what is the one big feeling of the brand?
Prompt → HTML: ask the AI for ONE single HTML file — hero image section, about section, price list in ₦, contact section. Save it and double-click to open it.
Generate the hero image or logo and put it in.
Make the 15-SECOND advert: a video with voice, OR your voice-over over a static image. Check the length.
Write your 5-line pitch: what it is, who it's for, why now, the price (a real ₦ number), one proof.
Paste everything into the submit box: the HTML (or attach the file), the advert's file path + duration, the pitch, your prompt log, and the list of AI tools you used.
Rehearse the 3-minute pitch once out loud. On stage: the site must open in under 30 seconds.
days.ifStuck: Build in this order — site, image, advert, pitch. If time runs short, a simple site + strong pitch beats a fancy site + no pitch.
days.ifEarly: Add a testimonial section to the site, or a short jingle over your advert's last 3 seconds.
doneWhen: The site opens — one HTML file, offline
The advert plays — 15 seconds, voice + music
The 5-line pitch is delivered, with at least one real ₦ number
deliverables: The site: paste the full HTML (or attach the file) and say where it's saved
The hero image or logo attached
The advert — file path or link, plus its duration
The 5-line pitch pasted
PROMPT LOG for the site, image and advert + the list of AI tools you used (at least 3)
caveats: Every asset is made TODAY inside the window — no recycling Week 1–3 work or class assets.
At least 3 different AI tools used — list them by name.
The site must be ONE HTML file that opens offline.
The pitch must contain at least one real ₦ number.
Demo rule: the site opens in under 30 seconds — no 'wait, let me boot something' on stage.
days.evidenceNote: Paste everything the grading agent reads: the pitch, the prompt log, the tools list, the HTML. Keep the site and advert open for the human judge.
